current.text: He signed a minimum contract to go back to Orlando.
Wendell Carter Jr. is Orlando's starting center and Vucevic is his backup. Goga Bitadze will still get some minutes.
Orlando added him to fix a bench unit that ranked 27th or 28th in scoring last season.
Expected to play about 20 to 22 minutes off the bench, down from 28. He is not expected to push for starter's minutes, and one expert says he could even be third string.
Can still score 12 to 14 points per game off the bench and is an upgrade on Mo Wagner.
Do not draft him at his ESPN ADP of 55 to 89 or as a starter in the top 80 to 90. He is a bad pick at that price.

Experts disagree on whether to draft him at all. Some say he is still draftable around rank 103 and is good value at the end of a deep draft. Others say not to draft him in 10, 12 or 14 team leagues, and Lloyd calls him cooked.
He could be top 100 if Wendell Carter Jr. gets hurt.
His assists last season were helped by luck: a 68% potential assist conversion rate.

durable.text: Pretty good passer for a big man.
He gets rebounds without blocks. He is the exception to the rule that rebounders also block shots.
Steals are his weakest category for a center. His FT% and low turnovers are good for a center.

note: He went for 17 USD in our auction last season. As a backup in Orlando he is now worth 0 USD on Yahoo (rank 177) and 2 USD on ESPN (rank 103), so pay 1 to 2 USD at most, and only as a late bench pick. He fits punt STL builds and gives a center's rebounds with good FT% and few turnovers, but blocks are thin. Early in the season, check his minutes against Goga Bitadze under new coach Sean Sweeney, and keep an eye on Wendell Carter Jr.'s health, which is his only real route to top 100 value.
